faqs.q: Sec. 38-161. - Determination and abatement of nuisances and nuisance properties.
faqs.a:
(a)
Legislative declaration.
It is hereby found and declared that certain structures or properties within the
               city have or may have become nuisance properties or may harbor nuisance conditions,
               with the consequent impairment of taxable values upon which, in part, municipal revenues
               depend; that such nuisances or nuisance properties are detrimental or inimical to
               the health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the citizens and to the economic
               welfare of the municipality; that in order to improve and maintain the general character
               of the municipality, it is necessary to rehabilitate such nuisance properties by eliminating
               nuisances within such areas for the protection of the health, safety, morals, and
               general welfare of the municipality, to preserve existing values of other properties
               within or adjacent to such areas, and to preserve the taxable value of the property
               within such areas; and the necessity in the public interest for provisions herein
               set forth is hereby declared as a matter of legislative determination to be a public
               purpose and a public use. Failure by any owner, agent, tenant, occupant, or other
               party in interest to comply with any provision of this article or with
chapter 3
of the I.P.M.C. is hereby deemed to be a nuisance and subject to enforcement as set
               forth herein.
(b)
Removal proceedings.
Except where this article provides otherwise, the provisions of article V of chapter
               2 of this Code shall govern the conduct of any administrative hearing conducted in
               accordance with this article.
(1)
Process.
Notwithstanding the commencement of any criminal prosecution alleging a violation
               of this article or the lack of such criminal prosecution, if the owner or occupant
               shall fail to remove or eliminate a nuisance or abate a nuisance property, the code
               enforcement officer may notify the city manager or a designee thereof who shall give
               ten calendar days' written notice to the owner, agent, tenant, or occupant and any
               other party in interest as determined from the records of the appropriate clerk and
               recorder to appear before the city manager or a designee thereof for the purposes
               of a hearing on a specified date to show cause why the nuisance conditions should
               not be removed or eliminated.
(2)
Notice.
The notice to show cause referred to in subsection
38-161
(b)(i) of this section shall be specific as to the nuisance conditions, shall state
               that the owner's property may be subject to assessment for all costs associated with
               removal, elimination, or abatement by the city of the nuisance conditions, and shall
               be served upon the necessary parties by personal service or by certified mail, return
               receipt requested. If diligent efforts to serve the necessary parties personally or
               by certified mail, return receipt requested, are unsuccessful, it shall be deemed
               sufficient notice if the above-mentioned written notice is mailed by first class mail
               to the necessary parties. In addition, a copy of the notice of hearing may be posted
               in a conspicuous place on the premises where the nuisance conditions are found to
               exist. No further notice shall be necessary.
(3)
Hearing.
At the hearing referred to in subsections
38-161
(b)(i) and
38-161
(b)(2) of this section, the city manager, or his designee, shall hear such statements
               and consider such evidence as the code enforcement officer, the owner, agent, tenant,
               or occupant, or other party in interest, or any other witness shall offer relative
               to the existence of and removal, elimination, or abatement of nuisance conditions.
               The city manager, or his designee, shall make findings of fact from the statements
               and evidence offered as to whether they shall be removed or eliminated. If the city
               manager, or his designee, determines that nuisance conditions exist and should be
               removed or eliminated, he shall issue an order based on the findings of fact made
               pursuant herewith commanding the owner, agent, tenant, occupant, or other party in
               interest to remove or eliminate the nuisance conditions.
(4)
Order.
The order of the city manager, or his designee, made pursuant to subsection
38-161
(b)(3) of this section, shall be a final decision and may be appealed to the district
               court pursuant to Colorado Rule of Civil Procedure 106(a)(4). Failure of any party
               in interest to appeal such order constitutes a waiver by him of any right he may otherwise
               have to contest the city's right to eliminate or remove the nuisance conditions from
               his property, and charge the resulting costs against him and/or the property.
(5)
Compliance.
If an order issued by the city manager, or his designee, pursuant to subsection
38-161
(b)(3) of this section has not be complied with within 30 calendar days after its
               issuance, the city, at the direction of the city manager, or his designee, may cause
               the removal, elimination, or abatement of the nuisance conditions. If the hearing
               officer finds that waiting 30 calendar days for compliance would cause significant
               harm to the public health or safety, the hearing officer may shorten the time for
               compliance to a period not less than five calendar days. In the event of such an order
               shortening the time for compliance, the hearing officer shall also specify the time
               within which the owner, agent, tenant, or occupant, or other party in interest shall
               have to appeal the order to the district court.
(6)
Failure to comply.
Any such owner, agent, tenant, occupant or other party in interest who fails to comply
               with an order issued by the city manager, or his designee, pursuant to subsection
38-161
(b)(3) of this section, shall be charged with all administrative costs and expenses
               incurred in the removal, elimination, or abatement of nuisance conditions. Such administrative
               costs shall include the cost of said removal, elimination, or abatement, inspection
               fees, postal charges, legal expenses, and other expenses as ascertained by the city
               manager, or his designee, which are the result of the enforcement of this article.
               All costs are independent of any other penalties and powers of the city as set forth
               anywhere in this code.
(c)
Collection of costs.
The manner in which all costs incurred by the city in removing, eliminating, or abating
               nuisance conditions are collected shall be left to the discretion of the city manager,
               or his designee. Said costs may be assessed against the nuisance property or may be
               recovered in a suit against the owner, agent, tenant, occupant, or other party in
               interest of the nuisance property.
(1)
Assessment.
If the city manager or designee thereof determines to assess costs against the nuisance
               property, a statement enumerating all such costs to be assessed shall be prepared
               and such costs shall be assessed against the nuisance property.
(2)
Procedure.
In the event the assessment is not paid, collection of the assessment may be handled
               pursuant to the provisions of
chapter 59
entitled "Municipal Liens."
(3)
Other costs.
Any code compliance administration service fees are in addition to the assessment
               set forth in this section.
(d)
Voluntary agreement.
Any owner, agent, tenant, occupant, or other party in interest of the nuisance property
               may enter into a written agreement with the city through the city manager, or his
               designee, to have the city remove, eliminate, or abate nuisance conditions, and to
               have the city charge the cost of said removal, elimination, or abatement against the
               property as a lien pursuant to the provisions of
chapter 59
entitled "Municipal Liens." The execution of such an agreement shall be at the sole
               discretion of the city and shall include as costs all administrative costs and expenses."
(
Ord. No. 4095, § 2, 11-19-2007
)
